claims.text: Equimolar WTaTiVZr has enhanced plastic strain and toughness relative to commercially pure tungsten under high-temperature plasma-facing conditions.
The WTaTiVZr alloy consists of equimolar proportions of W, Ta, Ti, V, and Zr.
The constituents of WTaTiVZr are refractory and relatively low-activation elements.
Temperatures approaching 900–1000°C are representative of high-temperature plasma-facing-component service.
A refractory high-entropy alloy can retain a stable single BCC solid-solution phase up to 900°C.
The multi-principal-element composition of WTaTiVZr produces more pronounced local lattice distortions than commercially pure tungsten.
The local lattice distortions in WTaTiVZr generate heterogeneous strain fields.
Local lattice distortions reduce the energy barrier for dislocation nucleation in WTaTiVZr.
Local lattice distortions increase dislocation mobility in WTaTiVZr.
Enhanced dislocation nucleation and mobility promote dynamic recovery and more uniform plastic flow at high temperature.
Dynamic recovery and more uniform plastic flow increase sustainable plastic strain and toughness in WTaTiVZr.
Under identical high-temperature loading, WTaTiVZr will develop a higher and more uniformly distributed dislocation density than pure tungsten.
Under identical high-temperature loading, WTaTiVZr will exhibit a higher dislocation-nucleation rate than pure tungsten.
Under identical high-temperature loading, WTaTiVZr will exhibit greater plastic strain than pure tungsten.
Under identical high-temperature loading, WTaTiVZr will exhibit greater toughness than pure tungsten.
Commercially pure tungsten has a high ductile-to-brittle transition temperature and is susceptible to radiation-induced embrittlement.
Commercially pure tungsten will show lower dislocation activity than WTaTiVZr under the specified loading conditions.
Secondary phases such as TiC, if present, could dominate the deformation behavior and limit the proposed mechanism.
Comparing only WTaTiVZr with pure tungsten under identical conditions isolates local lattice distortion as the cause of any mechanical differences.
A refractory single-phase HEA can exhibit high yield strength, excellent room-temperature plasticity, and resistance to softening at elevated temperatures.
